howto.name: Add the PDF
howto.text: Drop or select a PDF up to 500 MB that has a text layer, such as a batch of invoices or statements exported from software.

howto.name: Enter the text that starts each part
howto.text: Type a word or phrase that appears on the first page of every section, for example Invoice Number or Statement Date.

howto.name: Choose case matching
howto.text: Matching ignores capitalisation by default. Turn on case-sensitive matching when the phrase also appears in lower case elsewhere and you want only the exact form.

howto.name: Split and download
howto.text: Run it. A new part begins at each page where the text is found, and the parts arrive in a ZIP.

faq.q: Where exactly does each split happen?
faq.a: At every page that contains your text: that page starts a new part. Choose a phrase that appears once, on the first page of each section, so the parts line up with the documents you expect.

faq.q: Why does it find nothing in my scanned PDF?
faq.a: A scan is a picture of text with no text layer to search. Run OCR PDF first to add one, then split the result.
Not by default: Invoice, INVOICE and invoice all match. Switch on case-sensitive matching when only one form should trigger a split.

faq.q: My phrase appears several times on some pages.
faq.a: That only starts one part per page, but a phrase that also appears in running headers or on continuation pages will create extra splits. Use a phrase unique to the start of each section.

faq.q: What happens to the pages before the first match?
faq.a: They are kept as the first part, so nothing is lost. If your phrase appears nowhere in the document, the tool stops and tells you rather than returning a single unchanged file.

faq.q: What is this typically used for?
faq.a: Splitting a single export that holds many documents — invoices, payslips, statements or letters — back into one file per document.

faq.q: What happens to my PDF after I upload it?
faq.a: It is uploaded over HTTPS and split on the PrivaTools server in isolated temporary per-request storage, using local libraries rather than a third-party service. Response cleanup removes the PDF and the result after your download is sent, and a background sweep clears anything an interrupted request leaves behind. Nothing is added to an account or file library.
